dublinCore.description: Interactive MicroSim that builds a Huffman tree one merge at a time from a preset distribution or from the character counts of a typed message, shows how each merge adds one bit to every codeword below it, compares the average code length L with the entropy H, the efficiency H/L and a fixed-length code, and encodes and decodes the message with bit counts and the compression ratio.
relation: Chapter 13: Multirate Signal Processing and Compression

searchKeywords: build a Huffman tree step by step

learningObjectives: Construct a Huffman code by repeatedly merging the two least-probable nodes and reading the codewords from the root
Calculate the entropy H, the average code length L, the efficiency H/L and the compression ratio against a fixed-length code
Verify the bound H <= L < H + 1 and identify the distributions for which L = H exactly
Explain why a prefix-free code can be decoded without separators between codewords
Analyze why Huffman coding is inefficient for very skewed sources and how coding blocks of symbols improves it
prerequisites: Probability of discrete events and the base-2 logarithm

misconceptions.misconception: The Huffman code for a source is unique
misconceptions.correction: Ties can be broken in different ways and give different codeword lengths, but every Huffman code has the same minimum average length
misconceptions.evidence: For the skewed preset the sim's tie rule gives lengths 2, 2, 2, 3, 3; preferring merged nodes in the ties gives 1, 2, 3, 4, 4; both have L = 2.2 bits/symbol

misconceptions.misconception: Huffman coding always reaches the entropy
misconceptions.correction: L = H only when every probability is a power of 1/2; otherwise H <= L < H + 1, and every codeword needs at least one bit
misconceptions.evidence: The two-symbol preset (0.9, 0.1) shows L = 1.000 against H = 0.469, an efficiency of 46.9 %

accessibility.screenReaderScript: A Huffman tree is built one merge at a time. Symbols sit in a row of circles with a table below listing each probability, the ideal length minus log2 p, the codeword and its length. Each press of Next merge joins the two least-probable nodes (ringed in gold) and adds one bit to the codeword of every symbol below them. A side panel compares the entropy H, the average code length L, the efficiency H/L and a fixed-length code, and the bottom panel encodes the message in the text box into a bit stream and decodes it again.

responsiveBreakpoints.description: Below 680 px the statistics panel moves under the tree and shows a compact three-line summary without the bar chart

controls.label: Source
controls.description: Chooses where the symbol probabilities come from: a preset table or the character counts of the message

options.label: Count the characters of my message

controls.label: Message
controls.description: The message that is encoded and decoded; in 'Count the characters of my message' mode its character counts also set the probabilities. Presets load a sample message.

controls.label: Next merge
controls.description: Merges the two least-probable nodes (ringed in gold) into one node

controls.label: Undo
controls.description: Takes back the most recent merge

controls.label: Reset
controls.description: Returns to the separate symbols with no merges

visualElements.description: Huffman tree drawn bottom-up with the leaves in one row, 0/1 labels on the branches, merged-node probabilities, gold rings on the next pair and gold edges on the newest merge; pointing at a leaf highlights its path
Code table aligned under the leaves: probability or count, ideal length -log2 p, codeword (with the newest bit highlighted) and length
Read-outs of H, L (or L so far), H/L, the fixed-length code and the compression ratio, with bars for H, L and the fixed length and the shaded band H <= L < H + 1
Encode/decode panel: the message, its bit stream with alternating colors per codeword, Huffman and fixed-length bit counts, compression ratio, and the decoded message

model.description: Huffman's algorithm on integer weights: repeatedly take the two smallest weights (ties: single symbols before merged nodes, symbols in alphabetical order, merged nodes oldest first), make them the left (0) and right (1) children of a new node; codewords are the branch labels from the root to each leaf
equations: L = sum_i p_i l_i = (sum of merged-node weights) / total weight
compression ratio = F / L = fixed-length bits / Huffman bits
algorithms: Huffman tree construction with a sorted queue
Prefix-free decoding by walking the tree from the root

instructionalStrategies: Predict the next merge before pressing Next merge
Compare each codeword length with -log2 p
Contrast typical and atypical messages with the English code
extensions: Add arithmetic coding of the same message for comparison
Add a block mode that codes pairs of symbols to show L per symbol approaching H
